reasoning: Prepared actions are validated before the closed four owner-list kinds are declared.
The first original reader must resolve its actual authorized personal home and request one of its declared home keys. Entity and other-home reads do not initiate prefetch.
The existing request-local queue retains the earlier version per database and key; each reader receives only its original references. Team references are resolved by their original reader.
No new owner lookup, timer, cross-request cache, multi-statement query or altered authentication boundary is introduced.
Concurrent mutation can keep an older revision, which is conservative and cannot acknowledge unseen data; missing or failed counters stay unknown.
The tests cover owner/database/request separation, unchanged team reference and row totals, original result projection, cancellation and fresh next request.
limitations: No claim that original Native 504 versus Web 480 SQL budget is resolved. New immutable-source Native run is required.

A later denied reader can leave a prepared same-home revision key unused. Reproduced late-issue denial adds zero SQL statements but one safe metadata key (52 parameter value bytes and at most 85 DataRow frame bytes); this is not zero-byte overhead for every failure.
Up to three planned keys can remain unused in other partial-failure paths. No additional keys are exposed in the successful sibling response.
No source-dependent authenticated PG pass is claimed locally; the existing mandatory isolated CI suite must execute the new case.
No production model or browser acceptance was run.
